## Extension blob storage SPI

Feature release. Adds a generic SPI letting third-party `GrimPlugin`
extensions store typed records and binary blobs alongside the built-in
datastore — without forking the backend layer or carving their own
table namespace.

## What's new

**`BlobStore`** — backend-agnostic binary blob SPI. Streaming `put` /
`get`, deterministic-key overload (content-addressed by SHA-256 of
bytes + caller-supplied namespace), namespace/prefix `list`, and
`BlobPutOptions` for compression and content-type hints. Backend
implementations stamp their `backendId()` into the returned `BlobRef`,
so blob references survive backend swaps without re-keying.

**`ExtensionDataStoreHandle`** — scoped per-extension handle exposed to
plugins via `GrimAbstractAPI#getExtensionDataStore(GrimPlugin)`.
`declareCategory(...)` for structured records,
`declareBinaryCategory(...)` for opaque bytes, plus `submit` / `query` /
`delete`, per-extension settings KV (`Setting.scopedTo(extensionId)`),
and `blobs()` for `BlobStore` access. Lifetime is tied to the extension's
`GrimPlugin` lifecycle so an extension unload also retires its category
declarations.

**`ExtensionStorageCategories`** — factory normalising category ids to
`ext/{extensionId}/{localId}`. Always implies
`Capability.EXTENSION_STORAGE` on the backing backend, which prevents
id collisions between extensions and the built-in `Categories.{VIOLATION,
SESSION, …}` namespace at declare time rather than at write time.

**`ExtensionStorageEvent` / `ExtensionStorageRecord`** — hot-path event
(mutable write slot) and immutable read DTO with `categoryId`, `key`,
`byte[] value`, timestamps, and optional `metadata` blob.

**`ExtensionStorageQueries`** — `GetLatest`, `ListByPrefix`,
`ListCreatedAfter`. Same shape as the built-in `Queries.*` so the
backend query dispatch is uniform across built-in and extension
categories.

**Session-attached blobs — actually wired up.** 1.3.x's `SessionEvent` /
`SessionRecord` carried a list-of-placeholder-records field that was
never functional: every bundled backend threw on non-empty lists. 1.4.0
replaces the placeholder with `SessionBlobRecord` (session-id, blob-ref,
metadata, recorded-at) backed by `BlobEvent` and surfaced through the
reshaped `Categories.BLOB`. The serialisation path is now implemented
on all six bundled backends.

**`Capability.EXTENSION_STORAGE`** — new capability constant. Required
by every `ExtensionStorageCategory`. Backends that haven't opted in
reject the category at `declareCategory(...)` time with a clean
`BackendException`.

## Breaking changes

Minor-version bump (1.3 → 1.4) for the following public surface
changes. The `internal.*` package is untouched; only `api.*` callers
need to read this.

- **`Categories.BLOB` reshape.** Was `Category<BlobRef>` with a
  placeholder factory that threw at runtime. Now `Category<BlobEvent>`
  with `BlobEvent::new`. Query result type changes from `BlobRef` to
  `SessionBlobRecord`. Callers using the old shape had a runtime error
  waiting for them; the type change is source-incompatible but
  runtime-compatible in the sense that no working code existed against
  the old shape.

- **Two unused placeholder model types removed** from
  `ac.grim.grimac.api.storage.model.*`. Both were artefacts of an
  earlier design iteration with no working backend implementation in
  1.3.x — the relational and NoSQL backends all threw on non-empty
  lists. Their role is now properly served by `SessionBlobRecord` +
  `BlobEvent`. If you were programmatically constructing instances of
  them (e.g. in a unit test), migrate to `SessionBlobRecord` and submit
  through `BlobEvent`.

- **`SessionEvent` / `SessionRecord` session-blob field.** The
  session-attached collection field is `sessionBlobs` with accessors
  `addSessionBlob` and `replaceSessionBlobs`. The prior placeholder
  field and its accessors are removed; the typed shape is now
  `List<SessionBlobRecord>`.

## Backend impact

All six bundled backends — `InMemoryBackend`, `MongoBackend`,
`MysqlBackend`, `PostgresBackend`, `RedisBackend`, `SqliteBackend` —
adopt the session-blob plumbing and now write actual `SessionBlobRecord`
rows. No schema bump on the relational backends: the pre-existing
`blob_*` columns on the session row carry the new structure; only the
serialised content changed, not the column shape. Existing 1.3.x
deployments boot under 1.4 without a migration step.

The `BlobStore` SPI ships with an in-memory reference implementation
suitable for testing. Production deployments will want an S3-compatible
or MinIO-backed `BlobStore`; a separate `grim-blobstore-s3` artifact is
planned for 1.4.1.

## Docs

`README.md` gains a section on **native `GrimPlugin` resolution** —
explains how `GrimAPIProvider.get()` finds the running GrimAC instance
across loader-boot ordering. The loader's stub classloader publishes
`ac.grim.grimac.api.*` before the resident jar installs, so
`GrimAPIProvider.get()` returning non-null doesn't by itself mean V3 is
enabled — call `isEnabled()` to disambiguate.

## Migration

Most callers won't need code changes. The session-blob plumbing only
matters for code that was constructing the prior placeholder type
(rare; nothing in the wild does this) or filtering on the prior
collection field.

Extensions wanting the new SPI should depend on
`ac.grim.grimac:GrimAPI:1.4.0.0` and call
`GrimAPIProvider.get().getExtensionDataStore(yourPlugin)`. See the
javadoc on `ExtensionDataStoreHandle` for the declare/submit/query
shape.

## Tests

- `BackendIntegrationTest` parameterised across all six backends —
  round-trip for `ExtensionStorageRecord` (`declare → submit →
  GetLatest / ListByPrefix / ListCreatedAfter`), `BlobStore`
  deterministic-key idempotency, namespace `list` correctness, blob-ref
  round-trip across backend restart.
- `SessionEvent` shape migration test on each relational backend —
  pre-1.4 fixtures with empty session-blob columns parse cleanly under
  the renamed field; non-empty fixtures (which previously threw) now
  round-trip via `SessionBlobRecord`.

## MariaDB support + MySQL prefix-LIKE perf fix

Drop-in 1.3.2.0 → 1.3.2.1. No public surface change. Two things land:

1. **MariaDB 10.6+ now actually works** as a `MysqlBackendProvider` target. Before, init failed at first DDL with a `MariaDB server version` syntax error because the v7 schema used a MySQL 8 functional index (`INDEX … ((LOWER(col)))`) that MariaDB doesn't implement (MDEV-22597, still open).
2. **`listPlayersByNamePrefix` on MySQL becomes O(matches) instead of O(table size).** The functional index path was never sargable for prefix LIKE — full table scan regardless of selectivity. Verified by EXPLAIN at 1M rows + measured speedup.

## What changed under `ac.grim.grimac.internal.storage.backend.mysql.*`

Both flavors now share the same v8 baseline DDL — a STORED `current_name_lower` generated column with a plain B-tree index — and the same read SQL. Only divergence left is the upsert syntax:

- **MySQL 8.0.19+** (`MysqlEightDialect`) — `INSERT … AS new ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = new.col`. Avoids the deprecated `VALUES()` form.
- **MariaDB 10.6+** (`MariaDbDialect`) — `INSERT … ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = VALUES(col)`. MariaDB never adopted MySQL 8.0.19's aliased-row syntax, so it stays on the legacy form (which it never deprecated).

Dialect is selected at backend init via `SELECT VERSION()` — same shape as the `SqliteBackend` legacy/modern dialect probe. Handles MariaDB's legacy `5.5.5-` compat prefix (MDEV-9788) so `5.5.5-10.11.16-MariaDB-…` parses correctly. Floors at MariaDB **10.6** with a clean `BackendException` if older — 10.6 is the oldest LTS still in upstream support, comfortably above the 10.2.1 floor for STORED generated columns and enforced CHECK constraints.

## Why the perf side existed at all

MySQL's optimiser refuses to use a functional index for `WHERE LOWER(col) LIKE 'prefix%'` — only equality (`= ?`) is sargable. EXPLAIN at 1M rows with `FORCE INDEX` still shows `type: ALL` for prefix patterns. The gen col shape gets `type: range` and scales with selectivity instead of table size.

Measured on `mysql:8.4.9` against a 1M-row `players` table:

| Prefix pattern | v7 (functional idx) | v8 (gen col) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| selective 5+ char (typical autocomplete) | ~1100 ms | ~1 ms | ~**1000×** |
| 4-char `play` (~2.6% selective) | ~1095 ms | ~1270 ms | ~0.85× — random-IO penalty for many row fetches outweighs the index range benefit at this selectivity |
| equality `getPlayerIdentityByName` | already fast | already fast | unchanged |

The dominant case in real usage (admins typing 4+ chars in slash commands, autocomplete after a near-full prefix) is selective, so the practical impact is "autocomplete that was unusable on 1M-row tables becomes instant."

## Schema v7 → v8 auto-migration

Existing v7 MySQL deployments auto-migrate on backend init via an additive `ALTER TABLE`:

1. `ADD COLUMN current_name_lower VARCHAR(32) AS (LOWER(current_name)) STORED`
2. `DROP INDEX idx_<players>_name_lower, ADD INDEX idx_<players>_name_lower (current_name_lower)` (one ALTER, no window without a lower-name index)
3. `ANALYZE TABLE` so the optimiser sees fresh stats on the new index

⚠️ **MySQL 8 requires `ALGORITHM=COPY` for adding STORED generated columns** — `INSTANT` and `INPLACE` both error out. That means a full table rewrite, **blocking writes for the duration**. Fine on alpha tables (~1 minute per 1M rows on NVMe SSD with default buffer pool) but if you're running a production-scale `players` table in the millions, plan a maintenance window or use `gh-ost` / `pt-online-schema-change` to do the rewrite online and skip the auto-migration.

No-op on MariaDB — the dialect was always at the v8 column layout in this PR's earlier commits, so its v7 schema already matched; the migration just bumps `schema_version`.

## Compat

- 1.3.2.0 source + binary compatible. No public method removed, no signature changed. `MysqlBackendProvider`, `MysqlBackend.ID`, `Backend#capabilities`, `Backend#supportedCategories` all unchanged.
- Existing MySQL deployments auto-upgrade on next boot. No config change needed (subject to the migration-cost caveat above).
- New MariaDB deployments — point `storage.mysql.jdbc-url` at the MariaDB instance exactly as you would for MySQL; the dialect probe handles flavor detection at init.

## Tests

- `MysqlBackendDialectTest` parameterised on flavor — fresh-DB v8 baseline round-trip. Identity upsert merging, case-insensitive name lookup, prefix search, session UPSERT, settings UPSERT on composite PK, paged violation reads. Both flavors green against the live `test-mysql-zone-a` (mysql:8.4.9) and `test-mariadb-zone-a` (mariadb:10.11.16) fixtures.
- `v7ToV8Migration` (MySQL only) — pre-seeds a v7-shape DB with a `CamelCaseName` identity row, boots the backend, verifies `schema_version` bumped to 8, the STORED column backfilled to `camelcasename`, the index now references the column not the `LOWER()` expression, and post-migration name + prefix queries find the row.
- EXPLAIN on MariaDB 10.11 confirms `idx_<players>_name_lower` is used (range scan for prefix, ref lookup for exact).

## Datastore + history v2

Adds the public surface for the database / history rewrite. Additive on top of 1.3.1.0 — no existing API class, method, or signature changed; existing consumers compile and run unchanged.

The Grim-side wiring (the `/grim history` command, alert routing, config parsing, plugin lifecycle) lands separately. This release is the API the wiring builds against.

## New

### `ac.grim.grimac.api.storage.*`

A `DataStore` facade with a category-routed write/read path, a backend SPI (`Backend`, `BackendProvider`, `BackendRegistry`) so addons can register their own engines, and the model + event records that flow through the rings.

```java
DataStore store = api.getDataStore();

// allocation-free hot path
store.submit(Categories.VIOLATION, e -> {
    e.playerUuid(uuid);
    e.checkStableKey(check.getStableKey());
    e.detail(verbose);
});

// async read
store.query(Categories.SESSION, Queries.listSessionsByPlayer(uuid).pageSize(20))
     .thenAccept(page -> render(page));
```

Categories shipping today: `VIOLATION`, `SESSION`, `PLAYER_IDENTITY`, `SETTING`, plus a `BLOB` category that's on the surface for forward-compat (no producer publishes to it yet).

### Backend SPI + capability validation

Backends declare an `EnumSet<Capability>` and the categories they support; the routing table is validated at startup so a misrouted `BLOB → SQLite` configuration fails loudly with a message instead of crashing on first write at 3am.

`Backend#getApiVersion()` is the contract version (separate from the on-disk schema version each backend owns internally) so backend impls built against an older API can be detected and refused on major mismatch.

### `BackendRegistry` on `GrimAbstractAPI`

```java
api.getBackendRegistry().register(new MyBackendProvider());
```

Addon-contributed backends register the same way the built-in ones do. The registry feeds the routing table.

### `AbstractCheck#getStableKey()`

```java
default String getStableKey() { return ""; }
```

The cross-version identity used by the storage layer — survives renames and removals so historical violations stay readable across plugin upgrades. Empty default means existing checks keep working; the runtime falls back to a `StableKeyMapping` table that covers the legacy display names.

### `HistoryService`

Returns structured `SessionSummary` / `SessionDetail` / `ViolationEntry` records. Rendering lives in each platform plugin, so a Bukkit plugin formats with `&` colour codes and a future Fabric plugin formats with `Style` builders, both off the same query path.

## What ships in `grim-internal`

The implementation jar carries:

- **SQLite** — phase-1 reference backend, ~1k lines, tested against modern + legacy SQLite dialects.
- **In-memory** — for unit tests and ephemeral configs.
- **Disruptor write path** — per-category ring with configurable wait strategy, batched commits, drop-on-overflow with rate-limited warns.
- **V0 → V1 migrator** — reads a 1.3.1-era `violations.sqlite` and replays the rows into the routed backend so `/grim history` is continuous across the upgrade. Idempotent + resumable; runs at startup unless `skip_migration: true`.
- **`BackendToBackendCopier`** — `/grim history copy <src> <dst>` for moving operators between backends without losing history.
- **MySQL / Postgres / Mongo / Redis** — skeleton impls, compile and wire through `BackendRegistry`. SQLite is the one I've shipped against in prod; treat the four networked backends as ready-to-iterate, not battle-tested.

## Build changes

JDBC and NoSQL drivers (sqlite-jdbc, mysql-connector-j, postgresql, mongodb-driver-sync, jedis) are declared `compileOnly` in `libs.versions.toml` so the consumer plugin picks which to ship in its shaded jar. An opt-in path also lets the holder plugin provide a newer `minecraft-{sqlite,mysql}-jdbc` than what's bundled.

`grim-internal` source compatibility raised to Java 17 — storage code uses records, sealed interfaces, and switch patterns. The public `api` module stays at Java 8 source compat as before.

## Marked `@ApiStatus.Experimental`

Everything under `ac.grim.grimac.api.storage.*` carries `@ApiStatus.Experimental`. The shape is what I want, but I'd rather have one window to react to feedback before locking it in for downstream extension authors. The intent is to drop the marker once the Grim-side wiring lands in prod.

## Compat

- 1.3.1.0 source + binary compatible. No method removed, no signature changed.
- Legacy `@GrimEventHandler` + `bus.subscribe(...)` paths unchanged.
- `GrimSetbackEvent` hierarchy from 1.3.1.0 unchanged.

## Tests

Unit + integration coverage in `grim-internal/src/test`:

- `BackendIntegrationTest` runs the same scenario suite against in-memory + SQLite (and is structured so a Mongo / Postgres / MySQL / Redis container can be plugged in).
- `SqliteBackendDialectTest` parameterised round-trip across modern + legacy SQLite dialects.
- `CheckRegistryTest` covers stable-key intern, collision-prefix disambiguation, and the v0 → v1 mapping fallback.

End-to-end on `paper-1.21.11` with the Grim-side wiring branch:

- `/grim history <player>` paginated session list with cursor-based paging
- `/grim history <player> <n>` session detail with violations grouped by interval
- `/grim history copy sqlite -> mysql` cross-backend migration
- V0 → V1 startup migration from a real `violations.sqlite` carried over from 1.3.1
- Crash recovery: `markCrashedSessions()` closes orphan sessions on next boot

All PASS.

## `GrimSetbackEvent` hierarchy

Additive release on top of 1.3.0.0. Fully backward-compatible with 1.3.0.0 subscribers; legacy 1.2.4.0 APIs remain deprecated-but-functional.

### New events

Three new observational events covering the "Grim did a setback" semantic — distinct from the packet-level `GrimTeleportEvent`, which wasn't a good fit for this audience.

- **`GrimSetbackEvent`** — abstract parent. Subscribe once, receive every setback regardless of packet type.
  ```java
  GrimSetbackEvent.Channel ch = (GrimSetbackEvent.Channel) bus.get(GrimSetbackEvent.class);
  ch.onAnySetback(plugin, (user, timestamp) -> { ... });
  ```
- **`GrimPlayerSetbackEvent`** — concrete, fires when Grim sends a player-on-foot setback (the `ServerPlayerPositionAndLook` branch). Carries `teleportId` plus destination `(x, y, z)`. The teleport id is identical to the co-firing `GrimTeleportEvent` at that site, so consumers can correlate by id.
- **`GrimVehicleSetbackEvent`** — concrete, fires when Grim sends a player-in-vehicle setback (the `ServerVehicleMove` branch). Carries destination `(x, y, z)`. No teleport id — the vehicle-move packet doesn't have one.

### Why two families?

`GrimTeleportEvent` (1.3.0.0) targets sibling anticheats that need to dedupe inbound teleport-confirms when their PacketEvents is shaded and Grim's outbound packets are invisible to them. That audience wants *every* outbound `ServerPlayerPositionAndLook` Grim emits — setback, AFK-bot probe, vehicle-replication fixup — correlated by id.

`GrimSetbackEvent` targets admin/observability consumers who want the *semantic* "Grim setback a player" signal, including the vehicle-move path that isn't a teleport packet.

A player-setback site fires both events; consumers subscribe to whichever framing fits.

### Bridge wiring

`GrimSetbackEvent` is an `AbstractEventChannel`. Subscribers at the abstract level automatically receive dispatches from each concrete child via the bridge-listener pattern already used by `GrimCheckEvent` → `FlagEvent`/`CompletePredictionEvent`. Zero-alloc hot path, no reflection.

### No breaking changes

- No existing event class, handler signature, or channel method changed.
- No deprecations introduced or removed.

Upgrade from 1.3.0.0 is a single-line version bump.

Rewrites event dispatch around per-event channels. Zero-alloc hot path,
typed handlers over positional fields, abstract-event subscribe via a
bridge-listener pattern. 1.2.4 source compat maintained.

## New

- **`bus.get(EventClass.class).onX(grimPlugin, handler)`** — the typed
  subscribe path. Handlers take the event's fields as positional args,
  no wrapper object, no registry lookup on fire. Every subscribe binds
  to a `GrimPlugin` so `bus.unregisterAllListeners(grim)` sweeps on
  plugin disable, same as Bukkit's `HandlerList`.

- **Abstract-event subscribe** for `GrimEvent`, `GrimCheckEvent`,
  `GrimVerboseCheckEvent`. Bridge-listener pattern installs concrete
  bridge entries into every child channel at subscribe time; the hot
  path stays untouched.

  ```java
  GrimCheckEvent.Channel abs = (GrimCheckEvent.Channel) bus.get(GrimCheckEvent.class);
  abs.onCheck(grim, (user, check, cancelled) -> {
      // fires for FlagEvent, CompletePredictionEvent, CommandExecuteEvent
      return cancelled;
  });

  // Root-level observer for metrics / debug:
  GrimEvent.Channel any = (GrimEvent.Channel) bus.get(GrimEvent.class);
  any.onAnyEvent(grim, (eventClass, cancelled) -> counts.get(eventClass).increment());
  ```

- **Addon events.** Plugins with their own event types call
  `bus.register(MyEvent.class, new MyEvent.Channel())` and, if they want
  abstract-level dispatch, `abstractChannel.registerSubtype(MyEvent.class, myChannel, MyEvent.Channel::bridgeFromCheck)`.
  Late registration after existing abstract subscribers is handled.

## Changed

- **Priority direction flipped.** Lower fires first, higher gets final
  say — Bukkit `EventPriority` convention (`LOWEST → … → MONITOR`).
  Pre-1.3 Grim sorted highest-first. Default priority (0) users are
  unaffected; callers with explicit priority numbers on
  `@GrimEventHandler` / class-keyed `subscribe(...)` should re-evaluate.

- `GrimEvent` gained a `CHANNEL` type parameter so `bus.get(Class)` can
  return the concrete channel without a cast at the call site.

## Deprecated (still works)

Every 1.2.4-style entry point is kept with `@Deprecated` and routes
through the same channels as the typed API:
- `bus.post(event)` — caller supplies the event instance; dispatch
  reaches both legacy-registered listeners AND typed handlers via each
  channel's `dispatchTypedFromLegacy` unpack method.
- `bus.subscribe(ctx, Class, GrimEventListener)` — class-keyed legacy
  subscribe, routes to the channel's legacy slot.
- `@GrimEventHandler` reflective annotated methods — scanned at
  registration, stored as legacy-slot entries.

Each concrete channel also exposes a `@Deprecated onX(Object ctx, …)`
overload that resolves a platform-specific context (Bukkit
`JavaPlugin`, Fabric `ModContainer`, raw `Class`) through the bus's
extension manager.

## Breaking vs 1.2.4

- **Priority direction flip** (see above). The only semantic break.

Three observational events added in the unreleased 1.2.5 development
version (`GrimTransactionSendEvent`, `GrimTransactionReceivedEvent`,
`GrimTeleportEvent`) have `private` constructors since they're now
typed-only. Never published, so nothing released breaks.

## No reflection on the hot path

`OptimizedEventBus` constructor explicitly news up each channel. Bridge
factories are plain static method references
(`FlagEvent.Channel::bridgeFromCheck`). `bus.get(Class)` is a
`ConcurrentHashMap` lookup. Obfuscator-safe: rename any event or its
nested `Channel` class and the bus constructor breaks at compile time,
not at runtime.

The only reflection in the codebase is inside the `@Deprecated
registerAnnotatedListeners` path, which only runs when a plugin opts
into `@GrimEventHandler` scanning.

## Benchmarks

JMH via `:benchmarks` subproject (task-local, not in the shipped jar):

| Mode | Subs | ns/op | B/op |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| typed | 0 | 2.17 | ≈10⁻⁵ |
| typed | 1 | 7.19 | ≈10⁻⁵ |
| typed | 3 | 13.51 | ≈10⁻⁴ |
| legacy | 1 | 15.05 | ≈10⁻⁴ |
| legacy | 3 | 21.99 | ≈10⁻⁴ |
| mixed | 3 | 18.39 | ≈10⁻⁴ |

`gc.count ≈ 0` and `gc.alloc.rate.norm ≈ 10⁻⁵ B/op` across every
configuration — the residual is JMH infrastructure noise, not dispatch.
Zero-alloc fire confirmed.

## Tests

21 unit tests covering priority ordering, typed/legacy mixed dispatch,
cancellation threading, pooled-event init, plugin-disable sweep,
reflective `@GrimEventHandler` plumbing, and the three non-negotiable
bridge-pattern cases (abstract-first, subtype-first, unsubscribe-sweep).

End-to-end on `paper-1.21.11`:
- `api-event-fire` — Join / Quit / Reload / TxSend / TxRecv typed paths
- `api-legacy-compat` — `@GrimEventHandler` still dispatches
- `api-flag-event` — Wurst Flight → cancellable `FlagEvent.onFlag(grim, ...)`
- `api-abstract-subscribe` — `GrimEvent.onAnyEvent` + `GrimCheckEvent.onCheck` fire via bridges

All four PASS.
